title: Reeds, mouthpieces and strengths he used
summary: Dejan talks about the reeds he used, mainly a three, sometimes a three and a half or two and a half, and how soft versus stiff reeds affect the lip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Speaking about clarinets, I wonder if you ever knew what these swells use

Well, I tell you, now I couldn't tell you which string he used, but he always told me, very seldom you catch two people using the sand and shredder reeds, they're like in the sandbag, and he said, very seldom, because sometimes he'd buy me a, I'd give him a little number two, and you'd have to make it, three, four, I'd get a number three, and you'd have to cut it down or something like that, you know, tell me a line, I'd just try to read, you know, some people, you know, just go by and shredder, you gotta by reading, you know, bring it down to ready warm, you know. Do you still do that, do you remember? You know, sometimes, I used to use a three and a half reed, and I don't know why, but sometimes I can use a three and a half, but most of the time I use a three, and sometimes I catch a tree running around the nose, most of the time, you know, late I catch some trees, but always use a violabrator reading, and always, to me, a violabrator, and all and every reed line, and the red line, and the dure and everything, but always can't be a flint, vibrate.
And did you use the same flint, you ever mean, you ever find that, you ever go?
Yeah, but a nut slant flint, you ever find it?
Well, what flint was you used to have a flint in it?
I used it about two and a half.
Oh, you were chopped to me.

Two and a half, but when I was playing a lot of numbers, like sometimes I would be playing simply numbers or something like that, you know, I was playing a soul kind of plug, I would try to work a three, another three out, you know, because it was easy to make the high notes. The soft reed, you gotta use your lip more, you know, tighten up and loosen your lip. The stiff reed, you know, you can play it more as well. I don't mean the two-step, I mean the one just about it. Yeah, I know.
I wondered if you ever knew what you were before, you ever have your notes?
No, no, no, no. I really, Thank you.
